title: Architecture document frontmatter
description: Frontmatter for a document under docs/architecture/, plus the element shape that carries the standard's two element-level obligations. Document status and element state are separate axes: a `current` document may be full of `proposed` and `unbuilt` elements, and is current precisely because it says so.

id.description: Stable document identifier. It does not change when the title or filename does.

type.description: Document category, from the standard's closed set.

status.description: Lifecycle state, from this type's controlled vocabulary. Agents do not invent statuses.

updated.description: Optional. Git already knows when the file changed; set this only where the document's own sense of currency differs from its last commit.

reviewed.description: Date a person or agent deliberately checked the document against reality and found it still true. Set it only where a review cadence has been declared.

owners.description: Who is answerable for the content. The first entry is the one answerable.

related.description: Declared relationships. Optional, so an absent relation proves nothing.

depends_on.description: Documents this one depends on. A separate field from `related`, not a relation within it.

supersedes.description: The record this one replaces. Reciprocated by that record's `superseded_by`.

superseded_by.description: The record that replaced this one. Reciprocated by that record's `supersedes`.

url.description: Canonical location, for a document that gets copied out of the repository.

elements.description: Machine-readable element declarations. Optional, because the standard declares element state at the smallest structure containing it, which is usually a section heading or a table row in the body. Where a validator extracts those, it validates each against `#/$defs/element` rather than against this list.

identifier.description: A document identifier such as SPEC-0012, ADR-0017 or ARCH-SECURITY.

target.description: A reference resolvable from outside this document: an identifier (SPEC-0004), a qualified identifier (lexicon:SPEC-0004), an issue or pull request (argus#142), or a repository-relative path to a document that has no identifier (docs/plans/2026-09-11-project-doc-template.md). A path target is never qualified with a repository prefix.

relatedEntry.description: One declared relationship, as a predicate and what it points at.

element.description: One architecture element and its state. `state` is a separate axis from the document's `status`: it answers whether the thing exists, not whether the document is current.

state.description: observed: verified to exist and behave this way. proposed: accepted in a specification or an ADR, not yet built. unbuilt: named so the map is complete, with no accepted specification yet.

governed_by.description: The specification or decision that accepted this element. Required at `proposed`, which is what separates an accepted intention from somebody's.

evidence.description: How the element was verified: a path, a test, a command, or a commit. Required at `observed`, because `observed` without evidence is an assertion. In diagram IR the same claim is carried by `sources` and `meta.repository`, which are that format's fields for it.

allOf.$comment: A proposed element owes the document that accepted it.
An observed element owes its source evidence.

$comment: `stale` is set deliberately, when a document is known not to match the system and cannot be corrected in the same change. The standard states no transition table for this type, so none is carried here.
